content.prompt: Find the area of the triangle formed by the lines $3x-2y=12$, $y=x-5$ and the:

answer.worked:
The two lines meet at $E$. Substituting $y=x-5$ into $3x-2y=12$:
$$\begin{aligned}3x-2(x-5)&=12\\x+10&=12\\x&=2\\y&=2-5\\y&=-3\end{aligned}$$
Thus $E=(2,-3)$. On the $x$-axis, $y=0$:
$$\begin{aligned}3x-2(0)&=12\\x&=4\\0&=x-5\\x&=5\end{aligned}$$
The other vertices are $(4,0)$ and $(5,0)$. The base is $5-4=1$ and the perpendicular height is $3$.
$$\begin{aligned}A&=\frac12\times1\times3\\A&=\frac32\text{ square units}\end{aligned}$$

Thus $E=(2,-3)$. On the $y$-axis, $x=0$:
$$\begin{aligned}3(0)-2y&=12\\y&=-6\\y&=0-5\\y&=-5\end{aligned}$$
The other vertices are $(0,-6)$ and $(0,-5)$. The base is $-5-(-6)=1$ and the perpendicular height is $2$.
